protocol.label_zh: 签名与 MAC 认证密钥交换

overview_classification.summary_label_zh: 模块格基、Loom-KEM 与 Shuttle 签名/MAC 组合的双向认证四消息 AKE

authentication.mechanism: Each party signs a role-separated KEM transcript with its long-term Shuttle key and authenticates its identity with a directional PRF-MAC.

roles.key_details: Holds a Shuttle signing key and creates a fresh single-use Loom-KEM pair (ek,dk).
Holds a Shuttle signing key and generates fresh KEM encapsulation randomness and nonce per session.

pre_distributed_material: Peer Shuttle verification keys or certificates supplied outside the four handshake messages

forward_secrecy.conditions: Claimed for fresh expired sessions in the post-specified-peer CK model, provided target session state/session keys were not revealed and all ephemeral KEM state was erased.

protocol_characteristics.key_confirmation: Explicit mutual confirmation through the two final directional MAC tags under mk_I and mk_R, together with role-separated signatures.
protocol_characteristics.transcript_binding: Signatures cover DTBS_I = 0 || sid || ek || ct_kem and DTBS_R = 1 || sid || ct_kem || ek; KDF+ uses K and nonce salt N_I || N_R.
protocol_characteristics.identity_binding: Directional MACs bind ID_I/ID_R to sid; signatures bind each role to sid and the ephemeral KEM transcript.

technical_classification.construction_paradigm: Four-message SIGMA-like Sign-and-MAC AKE using a strictly ephemeral rigid IND-CPAF Loom-KEM and long-term Shuttle signatures.

underlying_primitives.name: Loom-KEM
underlying_primitives.role: Strictly single-use ephemeral KEM, analyzed under IND-CPAF with rigidity

underlying_primitives.name: Shuttle
underlying_primitives.role: Long-term EUF-CMA signature for mutual transcript authentication

underlying_primitives.name: KDF+ and PRF-MAC
underlying_primitives.role: Session key, directional MAC-key derivation, identity binding, and explicit confirmation

security_models: IND-CPAF with one failure bit per ephemeral key

protocol_flow.semantics: Initiator creates a fresh single-use KEM key pair and sends the public key, SPI, and nonce.

components.name: ct_kem
components.semantics: Loom-KEM ciphertext including the CPAF rigidity tag.

protocol_flow.semantics: Responder encapsulates K to ek and returns the completed session identifier, ciphertext, and nonce.

components.name: ID_I
components.semantics: Initiator identity with two-byte length prefix.

components.name: tau_I
components.semantics: MAC under directional key mk_I over role, sid, and ID_I.

protocol_flow.semantics: After rigid decapsulation and KDF+, the initiator authenticates its role, transcript, and identity.

components.name: ID_R
components.semantics: Responder identity with two-byte length prefix.

components.name: tau_R
components.semantics: MAC under directional key mk_R over role, sid, and ID_R.

protocol_flow.semantics: Responder verifies the initiator, then returns its own signature and MAC; the initiator accepts only after verifying both.

static_contributions: Long-term Shuttle signing keys authenticate the transcript but do not contribute to K or SS.
key_schedule.transcript_hash: No single transcript hash in the KDF: transcript authentication is by DTBS_I = 0 || sid || ek || ct_kem and DTBS_R = 1 || sid || ct_kem || ek; the salt is N_I || N_R.
key_schedule.session_key_derivation: KDF+ chains SS = KDF(K, salt || 0x01), mk_I = KDF(K, SS || salt || 0x02), mk_R = KDF(K, mk_I || salt || 0x03), where salt = N_I || N_R.
key_schedule.domain_separation: Suffixes 0x01/0x02/0x03 separate SS, mk_I, and mk_R; role octets 0/1 separate initiator/responder signatures and MACs.
key_schedule.ephemeral_secret_erasure: dk must be erased immediately after its single decapsulation attempt, success or failure; responder encapsulation randomness and raw K are erased after key derivation.

parameter_sets.name: Loom-AKE-256
issues: The two authentication messages exceed a standard 1500-byte MTU and require fragmentation or application-layer chunking in UDP deployments.

parameter_sets.name: Loom-AKE-512
issues: All four messages exceed a standard 1500-byte MTU once ordinary transport overhead is included.

correctness.relationship: Each session makes one strictly single-use KEM decapsulation; an honest KEM decryption error is explicitly detected and aborts the session, so the session failure rate is the Loom-KEM DFR plus the negligible rigidity-tag error.
correctness.basis: Algorithm specification Tables 4-5 and Section 3.3, pp. 16-20.

security_claims.claim: Mutual authentication uses EUF-CMA signatures over role-separated KEM transcripts and directional PRF-MACs over identities.
Session-key security in the post-specified-peer Canetti-Krawczyk model despite the controlled non-negligible DFR.
security_claims.comparison_scope: Under IND-CPAF, rigidity, signature, MAC, and KDF assumptions

security_claims.claim: Perfect forward secrecy for fresh expired sessions because long-term signature keys are isolated from KEM/KDF key material.
security_claims.comparison_scope: Subject to erasure and CK freshness conditions

security_claims.claim: Single-use ephemeral decapsulation limits visible failure leakage to one accept/reject bit, modeled by IND-CPAF.
security_claims.comparison_scope: Only when each dk processes at most one ciphertext

claimed_advantages.claim: Compact initial KEM flights are designed to avoid IP fragmentation and fragmentation-based DoS exposure at selected MTU targets.
claimed_advantages.comparison_scope: Loom-AKE-128 under IPv6 minimum MTU; Loom-AKE-256 KEM flights under 1500-byte MTU

claimed_advantages.claim: Rigid IND-CPAF decapsulation avoids FO re-encryption and is reported to give about a fourfold decapsulation speedup.
Long-term signature authentication preserves compatibility with CA/X.509-style PKI and allows KEM/signature agility.
Key isolation provides PFS under the stated post-specified-peer CK model.

limitations_and_constraints.description: Loom deliberately permits non-negligible DFR (approximately 2^-18.9 to 2^-24.8); failures cause explicit session abort and may require bounded retry.
Each Loom-KEM key pair is single-use; reuse permits repeated failure-oracle observations and may enable key recovery.
dk must be zeroized after the first decapsulation attempt whether it succeeds or fails.
Loom-AKE-256 authentication messages and all Loom-AKE-512 messages exceed a standard 1500-byte MTU and require fragmentation or chunking in UDP deployments.
Implementations without dedicated countermeasures are expected to remain vulnerable to power/EM leakage, and variable-latency microarchitectural effects require platform-specific review.
Reported x86-64 measurements come from one Intel Core i7-14700 under Ubuntu 24.04/WSL2; each algorithm was measured in one benchmark session.
